text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Several people are injured in western Kenya when police disperse a crowd demonstrating against police brutality.
- Wildlife experts warn of dire consequences if game hunting or ivory trade are allowed again in Africa.
- Langata opposition member of parliament says he plans to push for support from Britain's Labour Party for constitutional reforms before Kenya's general election.
- President Daniel arap Moi says those clamouring for hurried change to Kenya's constitution are bent on introducing civil strife.
- British businessman John Ward, father of Julie Ward who was murdered more than eight years ago, says his daughters' killers are known but there is litle evidence to sustain a prosecution.
- A gang of cattle rustlers kill three people and torch 300 houses in the Rift Valley.
- The government imposes an immediate ban on the sale of fixed assets owned by all local authorities in the country.
- Nairobi police introduce a pilot community vigilante project to counter rising crime rate in the city centre. ($1=54 Kenya Shillings)
